description: Disabling foreach optimizer updates and adding activation checkpointing reduced the recorded peak below 22 GB.

notes: Peak 22.9 GB occurs both before first optimizer step (event 3164) and during later optimizer steps (events 6149, 6151). The foreach temporaries contribute to optimizer-step peaks; disabling foreach targets those recurrences.
Model parameters are 1.1B (width=2048, depth=34 from source), not 30B as untrusted nano interpretation suggests. Param memory 4.56 GB matches fp32 1.1B params.
AdamW moments (2×4.57 GB) account for 9.13 GB persistent optimizer_state. This is required and not reducible without policy change.
Activation memory is only 33 MB (stk_74abca1986ce4bc8); gradient checkpointing or microbatching would yield negligible savings.
Estimated 1.0 GB saving from disabling foreach is a hypothesis for host verification; overlapping savings with other optimizations not estimated.

root_causes.title: AdamW foreach temporary tensor lists (_foreach_sqrt, _foreach_addcdiv, etc.)
Unaccounted peak memory (fragmentation, allocator overhead, or unclassified allocations)

limitations: This is the historical fp32 result with tolerance-based comparison, not a bit-identical strict result or a bf16 trade-off run.
The historical loss comparison is recorded, but runtime pairing checks for inputs, effective batch and objective were not established.
Losses matched within tolerance; they were not bit-identical.
Retrieved documentation was not matched to the installed PyTorch version.
